When Musa said that to him, Fir'awn turned away entirely from that, looking with an eye of contempt and disdain, and said: ﴿"Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for some years of your life? When Pharaoh's proof had been established against him through clear argument and reason, he turned instead to overpowering Moses by his hand and his authority. He thought that beyond this position there was no further speech, so he said: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ At that, Moses said: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, with a decisive and manifest proof.

﴿He said: "Then bring it, if you are among the truthful." So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent.﴾ That is, plainly visible and clear, in the utmost of evidentness, clarity and magnitude, having legs and a large mouth, and a terrifying, alarming form.

﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ That is, from his pocket. ﴿And behold, it was white to the onlookers.﴾ That is, it shone like a piece of the moon. Then Pharaoh, by his wretchedness, hastened to denial and obstinacy, and said to the chiefs around him: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowledgeable sorcerer.﴾ That is, an accomplished expert skilled in magic. Pharaoh thus deceived them into thinking that this was of the kind of magic and not of the kind of miracle. Then he stirred them up and urged them to oppose him and disbelieve in him. He said: ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?﴾ That is, he wants to win people's hearts to himself through this, so that his helpers, supporters and followers multiply, and he overcomes you in your dominion, and takes the lands from you. So advise me about him: what should I do with him?

﴿They said: "Put him off, and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers who will bring you every knowledgeable sorcerer."﴾ [That is: delay him and his brother until you assemble for him from the cities of your kingdom and the provinces of your realm every knowledgeable sorcerer,] who will confront him and bring the like of what he has brought, so that you will prevail over him, and victory and support will be yours. He agreed to them in this. This was by the arrangement of God Most High for them in this matter, so that the people would gather on one open plain, and so that God's signs, proofs and demonstrations would become manifest to the people in the daytime, openly.

﴿They said: "Put him off, and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers who will bring you every knowledgeable sorcerer."﴾ [That is: delay him and his brother until you assemble for him from the cities of your kingdom and the provinces of your realm every knowledgeable sorcerer,] who will confront him and bring the like of what he has brought, so that you will prevail over him, and victory and support will be yours. He agreed to them in this. This was by the arrangement of God Most High for them in this matter, so that the people would gather on one open plain, and so that God's signs, proofs and demonstrations would become manifest to the people in the daytime, openly.

When Pharaoh's proof had been established against him through clear argument and reason, he turned instead to overpowering Moses by his hand and his authority. He thought that beyond this position there was no further speech, so he said: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ At that, Moses said: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, with a decisive and manifest proof.

﴿He said: "Then bring it, if you are among the truthful." So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent.﴾ That is, plainly visible and clear, in the utmost of evidentness, clarity and magnitude, having legs and a large mouth, and a terrifying, alarming form.

﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ That is, from his pocket. ﴿And behold, it was white to the onlookers.﴾ That is, it shone like a piece of the moon. Then Pharaoh, by his wretchedness, hastened to denial and obstinacy, and said to the chiefs around him: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowledgeable sorcerer.﴾ That is, an accomplished expert skilled in magic. Pharaoh thus deceived them into thinking that this was of the kind of magic and not of the kind of miracle. Then he stirred them up and urged them to oppose him and disbelieve in him. He said: ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?﴾ That is, he wants to win people's hearts to himself through this, so that his helpers, supporters and followers multiply, and he overcomes you in your dominion, and takes the lands from you. Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned this practical debate between Musa (Moses) and the Copts in *Surat al-A'raf*, in *Surat Ta-Ha*, and in this surah. The reason is that the Copts wanted to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refused except to perfect His light, "even though the disbelievers dislike it." This is the nature of disbelief and faith: whenever the two confront each other and face off, faith prevails. ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 18]. ﴿And say: "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish"﴾ [Al-Isra: 81].

For this reason, when the magicians came, Pharaoh had gathered them from the regions of the land of Egypt. At that time they were the most skilled and adept of people in magic and the most proficient in creating illusions. The magicians were a great multitude and a vast host. It was said that they numbered twelve thousand. It was said fifteen thousand. It was said seventeen thousand, and it was said nineteen thousand. It was said some thirty-odd thousand, and it was said eighty thousand. Other figures were also mentioned, and Allah knows best their number.

Ibn Ishaq said: Their affair rested with four of them, who were their leaders. They were Sawtar, 'Azur, Hatahat [in MS A: "Hatahah"], and Yasqa.

The people exerted themselves to gather that day, and one of them said: ﴿Perhaps we will follow the magicians if they are the victors. [He said: "Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near."]﴾ [Note: the bracketed Qur'anic words are an addition from MS F.] They did not say, "We will follow the truth, whether it comes from the magicians or from Musa." Rather, the subjects follow the religion of their king.

﴿Then when the magicians came﴾, meaning, to the assembly of Pharaoh, where he had set up a pavilion and gathered his retinue, his servants, his commanders [MS A addition], his viziers, the leaders of his state, and the soldiers of his kingdom. The magicians stood before Pharaoh, seeking from him kindness toward them and closeness to him if they prevailed. That is, this is what we have been gathered for. So they said: ﴿Will we surely have a reward if we are the victors?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near.﴾ That is, and more than what you ask, I will make you among those closest to me and my companions. Then they returned to the place of the debate and ﴿said: "O Musa, either you throw first, or we will be the first to throw." He said: "Rather, you throw."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 65–66]. This was abbreviated here, and Musa said to them: ﴿Throw what you are going to throw﴾. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staves, and said: "By the might of Pharaoh, we are indeed the victors."﴾

This is like what ignorant commoners say when they do something: "This is by the blessing of so-and-so."

Allah mentioned in *Surat al-A'raf* that they ﴿bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and produced a great magic﴾ [Al-A'raf: 116]. And He said in *Surat Ta-Ha*: ﴿Then behold, their ropes and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they were moving. So Musa felt a fear within himself. We said: "Do not fear, indeed you are the superior. And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician does not succeed wherever he comes."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66–69].

Here He said: ﴿So Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed what they had faked﴾, meaning it seized it, gathered it from every place, and swallowed it, leaving nothing of it behind.

Allah said: ﴿So the truth came to pass, and what they used to do was nullified. They were defeated there and turned back humiliated. And the magicians fell down prostrating. They said: "We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 118–122]. This was a very great matter, a decisive proof that cut off every excuse and a crushing argument. Those whom he had sought help from and asked to prevail had been defeated, had submitted, and at that very moment believed in Musa, and prostrated to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who sent Musa and Harun with the truth and with the dazzling miracle. Pharaoh was thus defeated with a defeat the world had never witnessed the like of. He was shameless and audacious against Him, may the curse of Allah be upon him. So he turned to obstinacy, stubbornness, and the claim of falsehood. He began to threaten and warn them, saying: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], and he said: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot you have hatched in the city to drive its people out from it, but you will soon know﴾ [Al-A'raf: 123].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 26, verses 60–68:

Many of the exegetes (mufassirun) mentioned that Pharaoh set out with a great army and a large host, [[In A: "كثير" (kathir).]] which refers to the entire population of the land of Egypt in his time: the people who bind and loose (ahl al-hall wa'l-'aqd), the rulers, the ministers, the nobles, the chiefs, and the soldiers. As for what many of the Israelite narrations (Isra'iliyyat, reports taken from Jewish and Christian sources) mention, namely that he set out with one million and six hundred thousand horsemen, of whom one hundred thousand rode dark-colored horses (khayl duhm), and Ka'b al-Ahbar (a Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of such reports) said: "Among them were eight hundred thousand dark bay horses (ahdam)," there is room for doubt about this. The apparent view is that it is among the exaggerations of the Children of Israel. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best. What He has informed us of is sufficient, and He did not specify their number, since there is no benefit in it, except that they all went out together.

﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾, meaning they reached them at the rising of the sun, which is its emergence.

﴿And when the two groups saw each other﴾, meaning each of the two parties saw the other. At that point ﴿the companions of Moses said: "Indeed, we are going to be overtaken."﴾ This was because their march had brought them to the shore of the sea (sayf al-bahr), which is the Sea of Qulzum (the Red Sea). The sea was in front of them, and Pharaoh had caught up with them with his armies. For this reason they said: ﴿Indeed, we are going to be overtaken.﴾ He said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ meaning: nothing of what you fear will reach you, for Allah, glorified is He, is the one who commanded me to march here with you, and He does not break His promise.

Harun, peace be upon him, was at the front, and with him was Yusha' ibn Nun, and [the believer from the family of Pharaoh and Moses, peace be upon him, were at the rear. Many of the exegetes mentioned that they stood still, not knowing what to do, and Yusha' ibn Nun] [[Added from F and A.]] or the believer from the family of Pharaoh said to Moses, peace be upon him: "O Prophet of Allah, is this where Allah commanded you to go?" He said: "Yes." Pharaoh and his army drew near, and only a little remained between them. At that point Allah commanded His Prophet Moses to strike the sea with his staff. He struck it and said: "Split open by the permission of Allah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hamza [ibn Muhammad] [[Addition from al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil (3/2/236) and al-Durr al-Manthur (5/86).]] ibn Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah ibn Salam, that when Moses, peace be upon him, reached the sea, he said: "O You who existed before everything and who brought everything into being, and who exists before everything, make for us an exit." So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Strike with your staff the sea﴾.

Qatadah said: Allah revealed to the sea that night: "When Moses strikes you with his staff, listen to him and obey." The sea spent that night in agitation, not knowing from which direction Moses would strike it. When Moses reached it, his young servant Yusha' ibn Nun said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, where did your Lord command you?" He said: "He commanded me to strike the sea." He said: "Then strike it."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Allah revealed to the sea, as has been related to me: "When Moses strikes you with his staff, split open for him." He said: So the sea spent the night striking its parts against one another, out of fear of Allah, the Exalted, and in anticipation of what Allah had commanded. Allah revealed to Moses: ﴿Strike with your staff the sea﴾, so he struck it with it, and in it was the authority (sultan) of Allah which He had given him, and it split open.

Many have mentioned that he gave it a kunya (honorific nickname) and said: "Split open for me, O Abu Khalid, by the power of Allah." [[In F and A: "بإذن الله" (by the permission of Allah).]]

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾, meaning like a great mountain. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others.

'Ata al-Khurasani said: it was the wide passage between two mountains.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the sea became twelve paths, one path for each tribe. al-Suddi added: there were openings in it through which they could see one another, the water stood up on either side like walls, and Allah sent the wind to the bottom of the sea, which dried it, so it became dry like the surface of the earth. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha: 77].

And He said concerning this story: ﴿And We brought near﴾, meaning there, ﴿the others﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata al-Khurasani, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said: ﴿And We brought near﴾ means: We brought Pharaoh and his soldiers close to the sea and drew them near to it.

﴿And We saved Moses and those with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others.﴾ meaning: We saved Moses and the Children of Israel and those who were with them in their religion, so not one of them perished, while Pharaoh and his soldiers were drowned, and not one man of them remained except that he perished.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud: that when Moses, peace be upon him, set out with the Children of Israel by night, news of this reached Pharaoh, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered, and then said: "No, by Allah, its skin will not be finished being stripped until six hundred thousand of the Copts have gathered to me." Moses set out until he reached the sea, and said to it: "Split!" The sea said: "You have been arrogant, O Moses! Have I ever split for any of the children of Adam, that I should split for you?" He said: And with Moses was a man on his horse, and that man said to him: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction," meaning the sea, so he urged his horse forward, it swam with him, and then came out. He said: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction." [[Added from F and A.]] He said: "By Allah, you have not lied, nor have you been lied to." Then he plunged in a second time, swam, and came out, and said: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction." He said: "By Allah, you have not lied [[In A: "ما كذب" (he has not lied).]] nor have you been lied to." He said: Then Allah revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff," so Moses struck it with his staff, and it split open, and in it were twelve paths, one for each tribe, which could see one another. When the companions of Moses had come out and the companions of Pharaoh had entered completely, the sea closed over them and drowned them.

In the narration of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, he said: When the last of the companions of Moses had come out, and the companions of Pharaoh were complete, the sea closed over them, and no greater mass of people was ever seen than on that day, and Pharaoh drowned, may Allah curse him.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, meaning: in this story and what it contains of wonders, victory, and support for the believing servants of Allah, there is a clear proof, a decisive argument, and far-reaching wisdom. ﴿And most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ Its explanation has already been given.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha: 77].

And He said concerning this story: ﴿And We brought near﴾, meaning there, ﴿the others﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata al-Khurasani, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said: ﴿And We brought near﴾ means: We brought Pharaoh and his soldiers close to the sea and drew them near to it.

﴿And We saved Moses and those with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others.﴾ meaning: We saved Moses and the Children of Israel and those who were with them in their religion, so not one of them perished, while Pharaoh and his soldiers were drowned, and not one man of them remained except that he perished.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud: that when Moses, peace be upon him, set out with the Children of Israel by night, news of this reached Pharaoh, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered, and then said: "No, by Allah, its skin will not be finished being stripped until six hundred thousand of the Copts have gathered to me." Moses set out until he reached the sea, and said to it: "Split!" The sea said: "You have been arrogant, O Moses! Have I ever split for any of the children of Adam, that I should split for you?" He said: And with Moses was a man on his horse, and that man said to him: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction," meaning the sea, so he urged his horse forward, it swam with him, and then came out. He said: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction." [[Added from F and A.]] He said: "By Allah, you have not lied, nor have you been lied to." Then he plunged in a second time, swam, and came out, and said: "Where were you commanded, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I was only commanded to this direction." He said: "By Allah, you have not lied [[In A: "ما كذب" (he has not lied).]] nor have you been lied to." He said: Then Allah revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff," so Moses struck it with his staff, and it split open, and in it were twelve paths, one for each tribe, which could see one another. When the companions of Moses had come out and the companions of Pharaoh had entered completely, the sea closed over them and drowned them.

In the narration of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, he said: When the last of the companions of Moses had come out, and the companions of Pharaoh were complete, the sea closed over them, and no greater mass of people was ever seen than on that day, and Pharaoh drowned, may Allah curse him.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, meaning: in this story and what it contains of wonders, victory, and support for the believing servants of Allah, there is a clear proof, a decisive argument, and far-reaching wisdom. ﴿And most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ Its explanation has already been given.

This is a report from Allah, exalted is He, about His servant, messenger and intimate friend Ibrahim (Abraham), the leader of the ḥunafāʾ (those who turn away from falsehood to pure monotheism). Allah commanded His messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to recite this account to his ummah, so that they would follow Ibrahim in sincerity (ikhlāṣ), trust in Allah (tawakkul), worshipping Allah alone without partner, and disavowing shirk and its adherents. Allah granted Ibrahim his right judgment (rushd) from before, that is, from his childhood until his old age. From the time he grew up and reached youth, he denounced his people's worship of idols alongside Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He said: ﴿What do you worship?﴾ That is: what are these images to which you are devoted?

﴿They said: We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them.﴾ That is: we persist in worshipping them and calling upon them.

﴿He said: Do they hear you when you call, or do they benefit you or harm you? They said: Rather, we found our fathers doing thus.﴾ That is: they acknowledged that their idols do none of these things, and that they only saw their fathers doing this, so they follow in their footsteps. At that point Ibrahim said to them: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: if these idols are something and have any effect, then let them inflict harm upon me, for I am their enemy; I do not care for them and do not give them any thought.

This is like what Allah says, reporting about Nuh (Noah), upon him be peace: ﴿So resolve upon your affair, and [gather] your partners. Then let not your affair be obscured to you; then carry it out upon me and give me no respite.﴾ (Yunus 10:71). And Hud, upon him be peace, said: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate with Him other than Him. So plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ (Hud 11:54–56). And thus Ibrahim disavowed their gods and said: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority?﴾ (al-Anʿam 6:81). Allah also says: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone.﴾ (al-Mumtahanah 60:4). And Allah says: ﴿And [mention] when Ibrahim said to his father and his people: Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me. And he made it a word lasting among his descendants that they might return.﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:26–28). That is: there is no god but Allah.

﴿He said: Do they hear you when you call, or do they benefit you or harm you? They said: Rather, we found our fathers doing thus.﴾ That is: they acknowledged that their idols do none of these things, and that they only saw their fathers doing this, so they follow in their footsteps. At that point Ibrahim said to them: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: if these idols are something and have any effect, then let them inflict harm upon me, for I am their enemy; I do not care for them and do not give them any thought.

This is like what Allah says, reporting about Nuh (Noah), upon him be peace: ﴿So resolve upon your affair, and [gather] your partners. Then let not your affair be obscured to you; then carry it out upon me and give me no respite.﴾ (Yunus 10:71). And Hud, upon him be peace, said: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate with Him other than Him. So plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ (Hud 11:54–56). And thus Ibrahim disavowed their gods and said: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority?﴾ (al-Anʿam 6:81). Allah also says: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone.﴾ (al-Mumtahanah 60:4). And Allah says: ﴿And [mention] when Ibrahim said to his father and his people: Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me. And he made it a word lasting among his descendants that they might return.﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:26–28). That is: there is no god but Allah.

Meaning: I worship none but the One who does these things. ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾: that is, He is the Creator who decreed a decree and guided creation toward it, so everything proceeds according to what has been decreed. He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills.

﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾: that is, He is my Creator and my Provider, through what He subjected and facilitated of heavenly and earthly causes. He drives the clouds, sends down water, gives life to the earth by it, and brings forth from it every kind of fruit as sustenance for the servants, and He sends down water sweet and pure, ﴿that We may give drink thereof to cattle and many humans, of what We have created﴾ [al-Furqan 25:49].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾: he attributed the illness to himself, although it is by the decree, the qadar, of Allah and His judgment and creation. He ascribed it to himself out of courtesy (adab), just as Allah the Exalted commanded the worshipper to say: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned Your anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah 1:6–7]. Thus He attributed the bestowing of favour to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, while the agent of anger was omitted out of courtesy, and the going astray was attributed to the servants. Likewise the jinn said: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those upon the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 72:10]. Therefore Ibrahim said: ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾, meaning: when I fall into illness, none other than Him can cure me, through the causes He has decreed that lead to it.

﴿And who causes me to die and then gives me life﴾: that is, He is the One who gives life and causes death, and none other than Him is able to do that, for He is the One who originates and brings back.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 26, verse 83–89:

This is a request from Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that his Lord grant him hukm (judgement, wisdom).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is al-'ilm (knowledge). 'Ikrimah said: it is al-lubb (understanding). Mujahid said: it is the Qur'an. As-Suddi said: it is prophethood. And His saying: ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾ means: make me among the righteous in this world and the Hereafter, just as the Prophet ﷺ said at the time of death: "Allahumma ar-rafiq al-a'la" (O Allah, the Highest Companion), saying it three times [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6509), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2191), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her. Neither of them has that he said it three times; rather, they indicate that it was twice, and Allah knows best]. And in the hadith in supplication: "Allahumma ahyina muslimin wa amitna muslimin, wa alhiqna bis-salihin, ghayra khaza-ya wa la mubaddilin" (O Allah, let us live as Muslims, die as Muslims, and join us with the righteous, without being disgraced or being led astray) [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/424) from the hadith of az-Zurqi, and in his version: "ghayra khaza-ya wa la maftunin" (without being disgraced or tempted)].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾ means: grant me a good remembrance after me, by which I am mentioned and in which I am followed in goodness, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations: Peace upon Ibrahim. Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾ [as-Saffat: 108–110].

Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾ means: good praise. Mujahid said: it is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27], and like His saying: ﴿And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾ [an-Nahl: 122].

Laith ibn Abi Sulaym said: every religion loves him and claims him. 'Ikrimah said likewise.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾ means: bestow favour upon me in this world by the continuance of a good remembrance after me, and in the Hereafter by making me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And forgive my father, for he is among the misguided﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. This is among what Ibrahim, peace be upon him, retracted, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Ibrahim's plea for forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing﴾ [at-Tawbah: 114].

Allah the Exalted has cut off the connection of his plea for forgiveness for his father, saying: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: "Indeed, we are free of you and of whatever you worship other than Allah. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone," except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father: "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power to do anything for you against Allah"﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾ means: protect me from disgrace on the Day of Resurrection, the day when all creation, first and last, is resurrected.

al-Bukhari said, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Ibrahim will see his father on the Day of Resurrection, and upon his face will be dust and darkness."* [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4768)].

Isma'il narrated to us: my brother narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Ibrahim will meet his father, and he will say: O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected. Then Allah will say: Indeed I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers."

This is how he narrated it at this verse. In the chapter on the prophets, he narrated it alone with this same chain, and its wording is: Ibrahim will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face will be darkness and dust. Ibrahim will say to him: Did I not tell you: Do not disobey me? His father will say: Today I will not disobey you. Ibrahim will say: O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected, so what disgrace is greater than my farthest father? Allah the Exalted will say: Indeed I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers. Then it will be said: O Ibrahim, what is beneath your feet? He will look and see a male hyena smeared with filth, which will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3350)].

Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman an-Nasa'i said in his Tafsir from his Sunan al-Kubra, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ibrahim will see his father on the Day of Resurrection, with dust and darkness upon him, and he will say to him: Did I not forbid you from this, but you disobeyed me? He will say: Today I will not disobey you in anything. He will say: O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected; and if You disgrace his father, You have disgraced the farthest one. Allah will say: O Ibrahim, I have forbidden it to the disbelievers. Then he will be taken hold of, and it will be said: O Ibrahim, where is your father? He will say: You took him from me. It will be said: Look beneath you. He will look and see a hyena rolling in its filth, and it will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire."

This chain is strange (gharib), and it contains a denounced element (nakarah).

The dhi'b (hyena) is the male of the hyenas. It is as if He transformed Azar into the form of a hyena smeared with its own filth, and so he is thrown into the Fire in that form.

It was also narrated by al-Bazzar from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and in it there is strangeness. He also narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, from Ja'far ibn 'Abd al-Ghafir, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.

* *

And His saying: ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ means: on that Day, a person's wealth will not protect him from the punishment of Allah, even if he ransoms himself with the earth filled with gold; and neither will children, even if he ransoms himself with everyone on earth together. On that Day, nothing will benefit except faith in Allah, sincerity of religion toward Him, and disavowal of shirk. Therefore He said: ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾, meaning: free from defilement and shirk.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: the sound heart is that which knows that Allah is true, that the Hour is coming with no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ means: one who bears witness that there is no god but Allah.

Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: ﴿with a sound heart﴾ means: free from shirk.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: the sound heart is the healthy heart, and it is the heart of the believer, for the heart of the disbeliever and the hypocrite is diseased. Allah said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

Abu 'Uthman an-Naysaburi said: it is the heart empty of innovation, at peace with the Sunnah.

(4768)].

Others said: they will be cast headlong into it (kubkibu fīha). The letter kaf is repeated, as one says sarsara (to roar). The meaning is that some of them will be thrown upon others: the disbelievers and their leaders who invited them to associate partners with Allah.

This is an announcement from Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, concerning His servant and messenger Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, who was the first messenger sent to the earth after idols and rival deities had been worshipped. Allah sent him to forbid that and to warn against the severity of His punishment. His people denied him and persisted in their evil deeds in worshipping their idols. Their denial of him amounts to the denial of all the messengers; for this reason He said: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers when their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ That is: will you not fear Allah in worshipping other than Him?

﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ That is: I am a messenger from Allah to you, trustworthy in what He has sent me with. I convey to you the message of Allah without adding to it or subtracting from it.

﴿So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for any payment for it; my payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: I do not seek from you any reward for my advice to you; rather, I store up its reward with Allah. ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ for my truthfulness, my sincere advice and my trustworthiness in what He has sent me with, and in what He has entrusted to me, have become clear to you and evident.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 26, verse 111–115:

They say: "Shall we believe in you when the lowest (al-arradhil) are those who follow you and affirm you, and they are our lowly ones?" And for this reason they said: ﴿Shall we believe in you, when the lowest have followed you?﴾ He said: ﴿And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ That is: what would be incumbent upon me from following these people for me, even if they were upon whatever they were upon? It is not incumbent upon me to probe into it, investigate it, or examine it. Rather, it is incumbent upon me to accept from them their affirmation of me, and to leave their inner states (sara'ir) to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ It is as though they asked him to push them away from him so that they would follow him, but he refused this of them and said: ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers. I am only a clear warner.﴾ That is: I was only sent as a warner, so whoever obeys me, follows me and affirms me, he is from me and I am from him, whether he be noble or lowly, or of high standing or of humble standing.

When the Prophet of Allah had remained among them for a long time, calling them to Allah by night and by day, openly and secretly, and each time he repeated the call to them, they persisted in gross disbelief and fierce refusal. At last they said: ﴿If you do not desist﴾, meaning: from calling us to your religion, ﴿O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾, meaning: we will surely stone you.[[In manuscript A: "we will stone you."]] At that, he invoked a supplication against them, which Allah answered. He said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my people have denied me. So judge between me and them with a decisive judgment, and save me and those with me among the believers﴾. As He said in another verse: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help me." So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down, and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed. And We carried him upon one of planks and nails, sailing before Our eyes as a reward for one who had been denied﴾ [Al-Qamar: 10–14].

Here He said: ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship. Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ Al-mashhun (the laden) is that which is filled with goods and pairs of animals, of every kind two, which were carried in it. That is: We saved him and all who were with him,[[In manuscript A: "We saved Noah."]] and [[In manuscript A: "who followed him."]] We drowned all who denied him and opposed his command. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾

They were at the height of physical strength, might, fierce force and great stature, and of abundant provision, wealth, gardens, springs, children, crops and fruits. Yet they worshipped others alongside Allah. So Allah sent to them a man from among them as a messenger, a bringer of good news and a warner. He called them to Allah alone and warned them of His vengeance and punishment should they oppose Him. He said to them what Noah had said to his people, until he said: ﴿Do you build a landmark on every high place for mere play?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 26:128].

You do this in vain, not because you need it, but merely for amusement, diversion and displaying your power. The commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 26, verses 136–140:

He, exalted is He, says, reporting the reply of the people of Hud to him after he had warned them, admonished them, encouraged them and frightened them, and had made the truth clear and plain to them: ﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers."﴾ That is, "We will not turn back from what we are upon." ﴿"This is nothing but the way of the former peoples, and we are not going to be punished."﴾ [Hud 11:53] "And we shall not abandon our gods for your words, and we are not going to believe you." [Hud 11:53] So it is with the matter in general, for God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:6] And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus 10:96–97]

* *

As for their saying: ﴿This is nothing but the way of the former peoples﴾: some of them read it, "in nothing but a creation (khalq)," with a fatha on the kha' and a sukun on the lam.

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Awfi from Abdullah ibn Abbas, Alqamah and Mujahid said: they mean, "What this (man) has brought us is nothing but the customs (akhlaq) of the former peoples." For this reason He said: ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

They were Arabs who lived in the city of al-Hijr, which lies between Wadi al-Qura and the lands of Syria, and their dwellings are well known and famous. We have already mentioned in "Surat al-A'raf" (at verses 73–78) the narrations reported about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passing by them when he wished to campaign against Syria, so he reached Tabuk, then returned to Madinah to prepare for that. But they refused him, denied him, and opposed him. He informed them that he did not seek any wage from them for his call, and that he sought his reward only from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then he reminded them of Allah's favours upon them, so he said:

He says to them, admonishing them and warning them of God's punishment (*niqam*) lest it befall them, and reminding them of God's blessings upon them in the abundant provisions He gave them and in placing them in security from what they feared. [[In the manuscripts Fa and Alif: "niqmatu" (singular).]] He caused gardens to grow for them [[In Alif: "al-habbat" (grains).]], made flowing springs gush forth for them, and brought forth for them crops and fruits. Therefore He said: ﴿And palm trees with their spathes soft and delicate﴾.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: "It ripened and reached maturity, so it is *hadim* (soft and delicate)."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And palm trees with their spathes soft and delicate﴾: "It means laden with fruit (*mu'shibah*)."

Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related from Amr ibn Abi Amr, who had met the Companions, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And palm trees with their spathes soft and delicate﴾: "When it becomes ripe (*rutab*) and loosens." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and said: "Something similar was also related from Abu Salih."

Abu Ishaq related from Abu al-Ala': ﴿And palm trees with their spathes soft and delicate﴾: "It is the *mudhannab* (the ripe dates that have begun to droop at the tip) of the dates."

Mujahid said: "It is that which, when pressed, crumbles, breaks into pieces and scatters." [[In Fa and Alif: "massa" (touched) instead of "kubisa" (pressed).]]

Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Abd al-Karim Abu Umayyah say: I heard Mujahid say concerning ﴿And palm trees with their spathes soft and delicate﴾: "When it emerges, you grasp it and it is crushed, so it is of the soft ripe dates, and of the dry brittle ones, which you grasp and it breaks."

Ikrimah and Qatadah said: *al-hadim* means the ripe and soft.

Al-Dahhak said: "When the weight of the fruit increases and the clusters of the fruit-bearing palm press upon one another, it is *hadim*."

Murrah said: "It is the spathe when it splits open and turns green."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It is that which has no pit (stone)."

Abu Sakhr said: "I have seen the spathe when the sheath splits open from it, and you see the spathe clinging together, part to part; that is the *hadim*."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And you hew out of the mountains houses, exultant﴾: Ibn Abbas and others said: it means skilful. In another report from him: *sharihin, ashirin* (greedy and insolent). This is the choice of Mujahid and a group. There is no contradiction between them, for they used to hew those houses out of the mountains out of insolence, arrogance and frivolity, without any need to dwell in them, and they were skilful and expert in carving and sculpting them, as is evident from their condition to anyone who has seen their dwellings. Therefore He said: ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾, that is: turn to doing that whose benefit will return to you in this world and the Hereafter, by worshipping your Lord who created you and provided for you, so that you may single Him out, worship Him, and glorify Him morning and evening.

﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant, who cause corruption in the land and do not reform﴾, meaning: their leaders and great ones, who call them to polytheism and disbelief and opposition to the truth.

The Most High says, informing about His servant and messenger Lut, peace be upon him, who is: Lut son of Haran son of Azar, and he is the nephew of Ibrahim al-Khalil (the Intimate Friend of God). God, exalted is He, had sent him to a great nation during the lifetime of Ibrahim. They lived in Sodom (Sadum) and its surrounding towns, which God destroyed, and in their place He made a foul, putrid lake. It is well known in the land of the Ghor, bordering the mountains of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), between it and the lands of Karak and Shawbak. [[In manuscripts F and A: "bayt".]] He called them to God, mighty and majestic is He, to worship Him alone with no partner, and to obey their messenger whom God had sent to them. He forbade them from disobeying God and from committing what they had invented in the world, which no creature before them had done: coming to males instead of females. For this reason the Most High said:

When the Prophet of Allah forbade his people from committing the abominations and from approaching males, and guided them to approach their wives whom Allah had created for them, the answer of his people was only to say: ﴿If you do not desist, O Lut﴾, meaning: from what you have brought to us, ﴿you will surely be among those expelled﴾, that is, we will banish you from among us. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 82]

When he saw that they would not refrain from what they were engaged in, and that they persisted in their misguidance, he disassociated himself from them and said: ﴿Indeed, I am of those who detest your deed.﴾ That is, those who hate it; he does not love it and is not pleased with it, so he is free of you. Then he invoked Allah against them, saying: ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾

These people, namely the Companions of the Thicket (Ashab al-Ayka), are according to the correct view the people of Madyan. The Prophet of Allah, Shu'ayb, was one of them, and he was not described here as "their brother Shu'ayb" because they were attributed to the worship of the Ayka, which is a tree. It is also said that it is a dense cluster of trees like a thicket, which they used to worship. Therefore, when Allah said, "The Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers," He did not say, "When their brother Shu'ayb said to them," but rather He said, ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them﴾. Thus He severed the relationship of brotherhood between them, because of the sense in which they were attributed to it, even though he was their brother by lineage. Some people did not perceive this subtle point and thought that the Companions of the Thicket were other than the people of Madyan, so they claimed that Allah sent Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, to two nations, and some of them said to three nations.

Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili, who is weak, narrated: "Ibn al-Suddi related to me, from his father, and Zakariyya ibn Umar [in F and A, "Amr"], from Khasif, from Ikrimah, who both said: Allah did not send a prophet twice except Shu'ayb: once to Madyan, and Allah seized them with the Blast, and once to the Companions of the Thicket, and Allah seized them with the punishment of the Day of the Canopy."

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrated, from Hudba, from Hammam, from Qatada, regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of the Rass﴾ [50:12], that they were the people of Shu'ayb, and His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Ayka﴾ [50:14] were the people of Shu'ayb.

Ishaq ibn Bishr said: Others besides Juwaybir said: "The Companions of the Ayka and Madyan are one and the same." And Allah knows best.

The memorizer Ibn Asakir also narrated in the biography of "Shu'ayb," through the chain of Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba, from his father, from Mu'awiya ibn Hisham, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Rabi'a ibn Sayf, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Madyan and the Companions of the Ayka are two nations, and Allah sent to both of them the Prophet Shu'ayb, peace be upon him." [See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (10/309)].

This is a strange report, and its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is questionable; the more likely view is that it is a statement of a companion (mawquf). The correct view is that they are one nation, described in every context by a single thing. For this reason he admonished these people and commanded them to give full measure and weight, as in the story of Madyan, "equal and alike" [in F and A: "sawa'"]. This indicates that they are one nation [in A: "this indicates that they are one"].

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 26, verses 181–184:

He, the Exalted, commands them to give full measure and weight (al-mikyal wal-mizan) and forbids them from cheating in them (al-tatfif fihima). So He says: ﴿Give full measure and do not be among those who cause loss.﴾ That is: when you give to people, complete the measure for them, and do not diminish the measure, giving them less while taking from them in full and complete when it is due to you. Rather, take as you give, and give as you take.

﴿And weigh with an even balance.﴾ Al-qistas (balance) is al-mizan (scale), and it is said it is al-qabban (steelyard). Some of them said: it is arabized from the Roman (Byzantine) language.

Mujahid said: "al-qistas al-mustaqim" means justice, in Roman (language). Qatadah said: al-qistas means justice.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not diminish people's things for them﴾ means: do not deprive them of their wealth. ﴿And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And fear the One who created you and the former generations.﴾ He warns them of the punishment of Allah, who created them and created their earliest forefathers, just as Musa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers﴾ [al-Saffat: 126]. Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿And he had certainly led astray from among you a great multitude﴾ [Ya-Sin: 62].

﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "A side of the sky." Qatadah said: "Pieces of the sky." Al-Suddi said: "A punishment from the sky." This is similar to what Quraysh said, which Allah reported about them in His saying: ﴿And they said, "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾, up to their saying: ﴿"Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us in group"﴾ [Al-Isra: 90-92]. And His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"﴾ [Al-Anfal: 32]. Likewise, these disbelieving ignorant people said: ﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are of the truthful.﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord knows best what you do."﴾ That is: Allah knows you best. If you deserve that, He will repay you with it, without wronging you. Thus it befell them as they asked, as a fitting recompense. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a great Day﴾. This was of the same kind as what they asked for, the falling of pieces of the sky upon them. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, made their punishment that they were struck by intense and extreme heat for seven days, from which nothing shaded them. Then a cloud came to them and shaded them, so they began to rush toward it to take shelter in its shade from the heat. When they had all gathered beneath it, Allah sent down upon them from it sparks of fire, a flame, and a great blaze. The earth quaked beneath them, and a great cry came upon them that took their souls. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a great Day﴾.

Allah has mentioned the description of their destruction in three places, each with a description suited to that context. In Al-A'raf He mentioned that the earthquake seized them, so they became prostrate in their homes. That is because they said: ﴿"O Shu'ayb, we will surely expel you and those who believe with you from our city, or you will return to our religion"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 88]. So they terrorized the prophet of Allah and those who followed him, and the earthquake seized them. In Surah Hud He said: ﴿And the cry seized those who had wronged﴾ [Hud: 94], because they mocked the prophet of Allah in their saying: ﴿"Does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped, or that we not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning one"﴾ [Hud: 87]. They said that by way of mockery and contempt, so it was fitting that a cry should come upon them to silence them. He said: ﴿And the cry seized those who had wronged.﴾[[In F: "So the cry seized them."]] Here they said: ﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are of the truthful﴾, in a manner of obstinacy and defiance, so it was fitting that what they considered unlikely to happen should befall them.

﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a great Day.﴾

Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar[[In F and A: "Amr".]] said, may Allah be pleased with him: Allah subjected them to heat for seven days, until nothing shaded them from it. This was also narrated from Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Allah sent the canopy to them, and when they had all gathered, Allah removed the canopy from them and made the sun intensely hot upon them, so they burned as locusts burn in a frying pan.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The people of Madyan were punished with three kinds of punishment. The earthquake seized them in their homes until they came out of them. When they came out, a severe terror befell them, so they feared to enter the houses lest they fall upon them. Allah the Exalted says: Indeed, the mention of this Qur'an and the praise of it are present in the books of the earlier peoples, which were transmitted from their prophets. They gave glad tidings of it in the distant and recent past, just as Allah took their covenant regarding that, until their last prophet stood up as an orator among his people, giving the glad tidings of Ahmad: ﴿And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad."﴾ [al-Saff: 6]. Here, al-Zubur means the books, and it is the plural of zabur (scripture). Likewise, al-Zabur is the Book of David. Allah says: ﴿And everything they have done is in the zubur﴾ [al-Qamar: 52], meaning it is written against them in the scrolls of the angels.

Then Allah says: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾. That is: Is it not sufficient for them, as a truthful witness to this, that the scholars among the Children of Israel find mention of this Qur'an in their books, which they study? What is meant is the upright among them, who acknowledge what is in their hands of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), his mission, and his community. This was reported by those among them who believed, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and Salman al-Farisi, concerning those of them whom they met and those like them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-Araf: 157], and the rest of the verse.

Then Allah the Exalted says, informing about the intensity of the disbelief of Quraysh and their obstinacy toward this Qur'an: even if He had sent it down upon a man of the non-Arabs, one who does not know a single word of Arabic, and this Book had been revealed to him with its clarity and eloquence, they would still not believe in it. For this reason He said: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it.﴾ As He informed about them in another verse: ﴿And if We opened for them a gate from the heaven, and they continued to ascend through it, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people bewitched."﴾ [al-Hijr: 14-15]. And He said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered everything before them, they would not have believed, unless Allah willed﴾ [al-Anam: 111]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. And even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96-97].

﴿They will not believe in it﴾, that is, in the truth, ﴿until they see the painful punishment﴾, that is, at a time when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.

﴿So it will come upon them suddenly﴾, that is, the punishment of Allah will come suddenly, ﴿while they perceive not. Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?"﴾. That is, when they witness the punishment they will wish that they were given a little respite so that they could act in obedience to Allah [out of their terror] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]]. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who wronged will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Had you not sworn before [that there would be] for you no cessation?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44]. So every wrongdoer, sinner and disbeliever, when he witnesses his punishment, regrets intensely. This is Pharaoh, when Moses, the one who spoke with Allah, invoked against him, saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, so that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment." He said, "Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾ [Yunus: 88, 89]. This supplication took effect on Pharaoh, and he did not believe until he saw the painful punishment. ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims." "Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters"﴾ [Yunus: 90, 91]. And He said: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 84, 85], and so on.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, is it of Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾: this is a denunciation of them and a threat to them, for they used to say to the Messenger, in denial and disbelief: ﴿Bring us the punishment of Allah﴾ [al-Ankabut: 29], as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾ [al-Ankabut: 53], and so on.

Then He said: ﴿Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them what they were promised, that which they were given enjoyment of will not avail them﴾. Ibn Kathir said: Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about His Mighty Book, which falsehood cannot reach from before it or from behind it, "a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy" (41:42). It was brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), who was strengthened by Allah, and ﴿the devils did not bring it down﴾.

Then He mentioned that it is barred to them in three respects. The first is that ﴿it is not befitting for them﴾, meaning that it is not something they desire or seek, because their nature is corruption and misleading the servants. This Book contains commanding what is good and forbidding what is evil, and it is light, guidance, and a great proof. So there is a great incompatibility between it and the devils. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it is not befitting for them﴾.

* *

His words ﴿nor are they able﴾ mean: even if it were befitting for them, they would not be able to do it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of Allah﴾ [Al-Hashr: 21].

Then He explained that even if it were befitting for them and they were able to bear it and convey it, they still could not reach it, because they are kept far from hearing the Qur'an at the time of its revelation. The heaven was filled with fierce guards and shooting stars during the period of the Qur'an's revelation to His Messenger (ﷺ). So none of the devils could reach the hearing of a single letter of it, lest the matter be confused. This is from Allah's mercy toward His servants, His preservation of His law, and His support of His Book and His Messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, they are removed far from hearing it﴾, as Allah, the Exalted, said, informing about the jinn: ﴿And we touched the heaven and found it filled with fierce guards and shooting flames. And we used to sit in some of its places to listen; but whoever listens now finds a watching flame lying in wait. And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [Al-Jinn: 8–10].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah al-Shu'ara' (26), verses 213–220:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding that He alone be worshipped, with no partner, and informing that whoever associates others with Him, He will punish him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In manuscripts F and A: "may the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him."]], to warn his closest kinsmen, i.e., those nearest to him, and that none of them will be saved except by faith in his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He also commanded him to lower his wing to those among the believing servants of Allah who follow him. As for whoever disobeys him among the creatures of Allah, whoever he may be, he should disassociate himself from him. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ This special warning does not contradict the general warning; rather it is one part of it, as He said: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and He said: ﴿So that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shura: 7], and He said: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51], and He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings with it to the righteous and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], and He said: ﴿That I may warn you with it and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], just as He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

In Sahih Muslim: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."

Many hadiths have been related concerning the revelation of this noble verse, so let us mention them:

The First Hadith:

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa and climbed upon it, then called out: "O sabahah!" The people gathered around him, some coming to him and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu Lu'ayy, if I were to inform you that there were horsemen at the foot of this mountain intending to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish all day! Did you call us only for this?" And Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4801), Sahih Muslim no. (208), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3363).]].

The Second Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." Muslim alone transmitted it [[al-Musnad (6/187) and Sahih Muslim no. (205).]].

The Third Hadith:

Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned [Quraysh] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]], addressing both the general and the specific, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. [O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. For indeed, by Allah, I possess nothing for you against Allah, except that you have a kinship which I will keep in good standing, with its moisture."

It was related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/360), Sahih Muslim no. (204), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3185).]]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." It was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Musa ibn Talhah as a mursal report, not mentioning Abu Hurayrah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/248).]]. The connected (mawsul) version is the sound one. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4771) and Sahih Muslim no. (206).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, buy yourselves from Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, and O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, buy yourselves from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you both wish."

He alone related it through this route [[al-Musnad (2/448).]]. He also alone related it, from Mu'awiyah, from Za'idah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording [[al-Musnad (2/398).]]. He also related it from Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it as a marfu' report [[al-Musnad (2/350).]].

Abu Ya'la said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Dhimam ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Banu Qusayy, O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd Manaf. I am the warner, and death is the sudden raider, and the Hour is the appointed time." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/10); Suwayd ibn Sa'id is subject to criticism.]].

The Fourth Hadith:

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq and Zuhayr ibn Amr, who both said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) climbed a rocky outcrop of a mountain, upon whose summit was a stone, and began calling out: "O Banu Abd Manaf, I am only a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy and went to warn his people, fearing they would be overtaken, so he began calling out and shouting: O sabahah!"

It was related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull al-Nahdi, from Qabisah and Zuhayr ibn Amr al-Hilali, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/60), Sahih Muslim no. (207), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11379).]].

The Fifth Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the people of his household, and thirty gathered, and they ate and drank. He said: "Who will take on my debts and my promises, and will be with me in Paradise, and will be my successor among my family?" A man, whom Shurayk did not name, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were a sea [...] who will undertake this?" Then the other spoke, and this was presented to his household, and Ali said: "I will."

[[al-Musnad (1/111). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Shurayk, who is trustworthy."]]

Another route, more detailed than this context: Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadhij, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, or called, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who were a group, each of whom eats a whole young camel and drinks a farq (a large measure). He said: And he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were satisfied. He said: The food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for a bowl, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched, or had not been drunk. Then he said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I have been sent to you in particular and to mankind in general, and you have seen from this verse what you have seen. Which of you will pledge allegiance to me that he will be my brother and my companion?" He said: No one rose to him. He said: I rose to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: He said: "Sit down." Then he said it three times, and each time I would rise to him, and he would say to me: "Sit down." Until in the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.

[[al-Musnad (1/159). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

A different chain, more unusual and more detailed than this one, with additional elements. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (*Proofs of Prophethood*): Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Someone who heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told me (and he asked me to keep his name secret) from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk, and lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what your Lord has commanded you, your Lord will punish you.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He called me and said: 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsfolk [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]]. I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you have been commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us, O Ali, a sheep with a sa' of food, and prepare for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib.'" [[In F: "for us".]] So I did, and they gathered before him. They were then forty men, give or take a man. Among them were his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab, the disbelieving wretch. I brought that dish to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece from it, split it with his teeth, then threw it around the sides of the dish and said: "Eat, in the name of Allah." The people ate until they were satisfied, and nothing could be seen but the traces of their fingers. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before. They ate until they were satisfied, and by Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared for us yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]], and they ate until they were satisfied. Then I gave them to drink from that cup until they were satisfied. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it and drink the like of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, indeed, by Allah, I know of no young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the affair of this world and the Hereafter."

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: "It has reached me that Ibn Ishaq heard it only from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/178).]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned something similar, but he added after his saying "I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter": "And Allah has commanded me to invite you to Him. So which of you will support me in this matter, on condition that he be my brother and such-and-such?" He said: "The people all held back from it, and I said, though I was the youngest of them in age, the most inflamed in eyes, the largest in belly, and the thinnest in shins: 'I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your minister in this.' He looked at me for a while, then said: 'Indeed, this is my brother, and such-and-such. So listen to him and obey him.'" He said: "The people rose laughing and said to Abu Talib: 'He has commanded you to listen to your son and obey him!'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/40).]]

Only Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam narrated this account in this form. He is abandoned (matruk), a liar, and a Shi'ite. Ali ibn al-Madini and others accused him of fabricating hadith, and the imams weakened him, may Allah have mercy on them.

Another chain: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us: al-Husayn ibn Isa ibn Maysarah al-Harithi related to us: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Quddus related to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food and a vessel of milk." He said: "I did so. Then he said: 'Call the Banu Hashim.'" He said: "I called them, and they were that day forty men, or forty and one man."
