He said: "Among them were ten who each ate a whole goat's leg with its condiment." He said: "When they brought the bowl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from its top and said: 'Eat.' They ate until they were satisfied, and it remained as it was, having lost only a little from it." He said: "Then I brought them the vessel and they drank until they were quenched, and there was a surplus. When they had finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak, but they hastened to speech and said: 'We have never seen anything like today's sorcery.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food." So I did. He said: "He gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, they hastened again and said the same thing as their first saying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said to me: 'Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food.'" [[In F: "for me" added.]] So I did. He said: "I gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened to speech and said: 'Which of you will settle my debt and be my successor in my family?'" He said: "They were silent, and al-Abbas was silent, fearing that this would consume his wealth. I was silent because of al-Abbas's age. Then he said it a second time, and al-Abbas was silent. When I saw that, I said: 'I, O Messenger of Allah.' [He said: 'You.'] [[added from F.]]" He said: "On that day I was the worst of them in appearance. I had inflamed eyes, a large belly, and thin shins."

These are multiple chains for this hadith from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. The meaning of his (ﷺ) request to his paternal uncles and their sons that they settle his debt and succeed him in his family is that, if he were killed in the way of Allah, since he feared that when he took up the burdens of warning he might be killed. When Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:67], then at that point he felt secure.

He had been guarded at first until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. At that time, none among the Banu Hashim was stronger in faith, certainty, and affirmation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Therefore he hastened ahead of them in committing to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked of them. Then after this, and Allah knows best, came his calling the people openly on al-Safa, and his warning to the clans of Quraysh in general and in particular, until he named some of his paternal uncles, aunts, and daughters, so that he might alert them to the greater by means of the lesser. That is: "I am only a warner, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path."

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi (not otherwise identified), through the chain of Amr ibn Samurah, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi, who said: "I saw Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, teaching people and giving them legal rulings, while his son was beside him and his family were sitting at the side of the mosque conversing. It was said to him: 'Why do people desire what you have of knowledge, while your family sit heedless?' He said: 'Because I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The prophets are the most detached from the world, and the hardest on them are the nearest of kin." This is what Allah revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾.'" Then he said: "Indeed, the people most averse to the scholar are his own family until he departs from them." This is why Allah (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk. And lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers. But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ [[Tarikh Dimashq (10/587, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ means: in all your affairs, for indeed He is your supporter, your helper, your protector, your victor, and the one who exalts your word.

* *

His saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: He takes care of you, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are before Our eyes﴾ [al-Tur 52:48].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: to the prayer.

Ikrimah said: He sees his standing, his bowing, and his prostration.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: when you pray alone.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: that is, from your bed or your sitting place.

Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you﴾: standing, sitting, and in all your conditions.

* *

His saying: ﴿And your movements among those who prostrate﴾: Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand, and your movements among those who prostrate﴾ means: in the prayer, He sees you alone and He sees you in congregation. This is the view of Ikrimah, Ata al-Khurasani, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Mujahid said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see those behind him just as he saw those in front of him. This is supported by what is authentically established in the hadith: "Straighten your rows, for indeed I see you from behind my back." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (723).]]

Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through two chains from Ibn Abbas that he said regarding this verse: it means His moving him from the loins of one prophet to the loins of another prophet until He brought him forth as a prophet.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ means: the All-Hearing of His servants' statements, the All-Knowing of their movements and stillness, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite of it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engrossed therein﴾ [Yunus 10:61], and the rest of the verse.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah al-Shu'ara' (26), verses 213–220:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding that He alone be worshipped, with no partner, and informing that whoever associates others with Him, He will punish him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In manuscripts F and A: "may the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him."]], to warn his closest kinsmen, i.e., those nearest to him, and that none of them will be saved except by faith in his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He also commanded him to lower his wing to those among the believing servants of Allah who follow him. As for whoever disobeys him among the creatures of Allah, whoever he may be, he should disassociate himself from him. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ This special warning does not contradict the general warning; rather it is one part of it, as He said: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and He said: ﴿So that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shura: 7], and He said: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51], and He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings with it to the righteous and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], and He said: ﴿That I may warn you with it and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], just as He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

In Sahih Muslim: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."

Many hadiths have been related concerning the revelation of this noble verse, so let us mention them:

The First Hadith:

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa and climbed upon it, then called out: "O sabahah!" The people gathered around him, some coming to him and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu Lu'ayy, if I were to inform you that there were horsemen at the foot of this mountain intending to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish all day! Did you call us only for this?" And Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4801), Sahih Muslim no. (208), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3363).]].

The Second Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." Muslim alone transmitted it [[al-Musnad (6/187) and Sahih Muslim no. (205).]].

The Third Hadith:

Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned [Quraysh] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]], addressing both the general and the specific, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. [O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. For indeed, by Allah, I possess nothing for you against Allah, except that you have a kinship which I will keep in good standing, with its moisture."

It was related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/360), Sahih Muslim no. (204), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3185).]]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." It was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Musa ibn Talhah as a mursal report, not mentioning Abu Hurayrah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/248).]]. The connected (mawsul) version is the sound one. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4771) and Sahih Muslim no. (206).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, buy yourselves from Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, and O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, buy yourselves from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you both wish."

He alone related it through this route [[al-Musnad (2/448).]]. He also alone related it, from Mu'awiyah, from Za'idah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording [[al-Musnad (2/398).]]. He also related it from Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it as a marfu' report [[al-Musnad (2/350).]].

Abu Ya'la said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Dhimam ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Banu Qusayy, O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd Manaf. I am the warner, and death is the sudden raider, and the Hour is the appointed time." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/10); Suwayd ibn Sa'id is subject to criticism.]].

The Fourth Hadith:

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq and Zuhayr ibn Amr, who both said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) climbed a rocky outcrop of a mountain, upon whose summit was a stone, and began calling out: "O Banu Abd Manaf, I am only a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy and went to warn his people, fearing they would be overtaken, so he began calling out and shouting: O sabahah!"

It was related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull al-Nahdi, from Qabisah and Zuhayr ibn Amr al-Hilali, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/60), Sahih Muslim no. (207), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11379).]].

The Fifth Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the people of his household, and thirty gathered, and they ate and drank. He said: "Who will take on my debts and my promises, and will be with me in Paradise, and will be my successor among my family?" A man, whom Shurayk did not name, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were a sea [...] who will undertake this?" Then the other spoke, and this was presented to his household, and Ali said: "I will."

[[al-Musnad (1/111). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Shurayk, who is trustworthy."]]

Another route, more detailed than this context: Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadhij, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, or called, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who were a group, each of whom eats a whole young camel and drinks a farq (a large measure). He said: And he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were satisfied. He said: The food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for a bowl, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched, or had not been drunk. Then he said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I have been sent to you in particular and to mankind in general, and you have seen from this verse what you have seen. Which of you will pledge allegiance to me that he will be my brother and my companion?" He said: No one rose to him. He said: I rose to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: He said: "Sit down." Then he said it three times, and each time I would rise to him, and he would say to me: "Sit down." Until in the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.

[[al-Musnad (1/159). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

A different chain, more unusual and more detailed than this one, with additional elements. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (*Proofs of Prophethood*): Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Someone who heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told me (and he asked me to keep his name secret) from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk, and lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what your Lord has commanded you, your Lord will punish you.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He called me and said: 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsfolk [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]]. I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you have been commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us, O Ali, a sheep with a sa' of food, and prepare for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib.'" [[In F: "for us".]] So I did, and they gathered before him. They were then forty men, give or take a man. Among them were his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab, the disbelieving wretch. I brought that dish to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece from it, split it with his teeth, then threw it around the sides of the dish and said: "Eat, in the name of Allah." The people ate until they were satisfied, and nothing could be seen but the traces of their fingers. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before. They ate until they were satisfied, and by Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared for us yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]], and they ate until they were satisfied. Then I gave them to drink from that cup until they were satisfied. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it and drink the like of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, indeed, by Allah, I know of no young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the affair of this world and the Hereafter."

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: "It has reached me that Ibn Ishaq heard it only from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/178).]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned something similar, but he added after his saying "I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter": "And Allah has commanded me to invite you to Him. So which of you will support me in this matter, on condition that he be my brother and such-and-such?" He said: "The people all held back from it, and I said, though I was the youngest of them in age, the most inflamed in eyes, the largest in belly, and the thinnest in shins: 'I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your minister in this.' He looked at me for a while, then said: 'Indeed, this is my brother, and such-and-such. So listen to him and obey him.'" He said: "The people rose laughing and said to Abu Talib: 'He has commanded you to listen to your son and obey him!'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/40).]]

Only Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam narrated this account in this form. He is abandoned (matruk), a liar, and a Shi'ite. Ali ibn al-Madini and others accused him of fabricating hadith, and the imams weakened him, may Allah have mercy on them.

Another chain: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us: al-Husayn ibn Isa ibn Maysarah al-Harithi related to us: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Quddus related to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food and a vessel of milk." He said: "I did so. Then he said: 'Call the Banu Hashim.'" He said: "I called them, and they were that day forty men, or forty and one man." He said: "Among them were ten who each ate a whole goat's leg with its condiment." He said: "When they brought the bowl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from its top and said: 'Eat.' They ate until they were satisfied, and it remained as it was, having lost only a little from it." He said: "Then I brought them the vessel and they drank until they were quenched, and there was a surplus. When they had finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak, but they hastened to speech and said: 'We have never seen anything like today's sorcery.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food." So I did. He said: "He gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, they hastened again and said the same thing as their first saying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said to me: 'Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food.'" [[In F: "for me" added.]] So I did. He said: "I gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened to speech and said: 'Which of you will settle my debt and be my successor in my family?'" He said: "They were silent, and al-Abbas was silent, fearing that this would consume his wealth. I was silent because of al-Abbas's age. Then he said it a second time, and al-Abbas was silent. When I saw that, I said: 'I, O Messenger of Allah.' [He said: 'You.'] [[added from F.]]" He said: "On that day I was the worst of them in appearance. I had inflamed eyes, a large belly, and thin shins."

These are multiple chains for this hadith from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. The meaning of his (ﷺ) request to his paternal uncles and their sons that they settle his debt and succeed him in his family is that, if he were killed in the way of Allah, since he feared that when he took up the burdens of warning he might be killed. When Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:67], then at that point he felt secure.

He had been guarded at first until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. At that time, none among the Banu Hashim was stronger in faith, certainty, and affirmation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Therefore he hastened ahead of them in committing to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked of them. Then after this, and Allah knows best, came his calling the people openly on al-Safa, and his warning to the clans of Quraysh in general and in particular, until he named some of his paternal uncles, aunts, and daughters, so that he might alert them to the greater by means of the lesser. That is: "I am only a warner, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path."

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi (not otherwise identified), through the chain of Amr ibn Samurah, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi, who said: "I saw Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, teaching people and giving them legal rulings, while his son was beside him and his family were sitting at the side of the mosque conversing. It was said to him: 'Why do people desire what you have of knowledge, while your family sit heedless?' He said: 'Because I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The prophets are the most detached from the world, and the hardest on them are the nearest of kin." This is what Allah revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾.'" Then he said: "Indeed, the people most averse to the scholar are his own family until he departs from them." This is why Allah (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk. And lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers. But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ [[Tarikh Dimashq (10/587, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ means: in all your affairs, for indeed He is your supporter, your helper, your protector, your victor, and the one who exalts your word.

* *

His saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: He takes care of you, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are before Our eyes﴾ [al-Tur 52:48].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: to the prayer.

Ikrimah said: He sees his standing, his bowing, and his prostration.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: when you pray alone.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: that is, from your bed or your sitting place.

Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you﴾: standing, sitting, and in all your conditions.

* *

His saying: ﴿And your movements among those who prostrate﴾: Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand, and your movements among those who prostrate﴾ means: in the prayer, He sees you alone and He sees you in congregation. This is the view of Ikrimah, Ata al-Khurasani, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Mujahid said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see those behind him just as he saw those in front of him. This is supported by what is authentically established in the hadith: "Straighten your rows, for indeed I see you from behind my back." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (723).]]

Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through two chains from Ibn Abbas that he said regarding this verse: it means His moving him from the loins of one prophet to the loins of another prophet until He brought him forth as a prophet.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ means: the All-Hearing of His servants' statements, the All-Knowing of their movements and stillness, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite of it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engrossed therein﴾ [Yunus 10:61], and the rest of the verse.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah al-Shu'ara' (26), verses 213–220:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding that He alone be worshipped, with no partner, and informing that whoever associates others with Him, He will punish him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In manuscripts F and A: "may the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him."]], to warn his closest kinsmen, i.e., those nearest to him, and that none of them will be saved except by faith in his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He also commanded him to lower his wing to those among the believing servants of Allah who follow him. As for whoever disobeys him among the creatures of Allah, whoever he may be, he should disassociate himself from him. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ This special warning does not contradict the general warning; rather it is one part of it, as He said: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and He said: ﴿So that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shura: 7], and He said: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51], and He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings with it to the righteous and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], and He said: ﴿That I may warn you with it and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], just as He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

In Sahih Muslim: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."

Many hadiths have been related concerning the revelation of this noble verse, so let us mention them:

The First Hadith:

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa and climbed upon it, then called out: "O sabahah!" The people gathered around him, some coming to him and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu Lu'ayy, if I were to inform you that there were horsemen at the foot of this mountain intending to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish all day! Did you call us only for this?" And Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4801), Sahih Muslim no. (208), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3363).]].

The Second Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." Muslim alone transmitted it [[al-Musnad (6/187) and Sahih Muslim no. (205).]].

The Third Hadith:

Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned [Quraysh] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]], addressing both the general and the specific, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. [O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. For indeed, by Allah, I possess nothing for you against Allah, except that you have a kinship which I will keep in good standing, with its moisture."

It was related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/360), Sahih Muslim no. (204), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3185).]]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." It was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Musa ibn Talhah as a mursal report, not mentioning Abu Hurayrah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/248).]]. The connected (mawsul) version is the sound one. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4771) and Sahih Muslim no. (206).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, buy yourselves from Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, and O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, buy yourselves from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you both wish."

He alone related it through this route [[al-Musnad (2/448).]]. He also alone related it, from Mu'awiyah, from Za'idah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording [[al-Musnad (2/398).]]. He also related it from Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it as a marfu' report [[al-Musnad (2/350).]].

Abu Ya'la said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Dhimam ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Banu Qusayy, O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd Manaf. I am the warner, and death is the sudden raider, and the Hour is the appointed time." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/10); Suwayd ibn Sa'id is subject to criticism.]].

The Fourth Hadith:

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq and Zuhayr ibn Amr, who both said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) climbed a rocky outcrop of a mountain, upon whose summit was a stone, and began calling out: "O Banu Abd Manaf, I am only a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy and went to warn his people, fearing they would be overtaken, so he began calling out and shouting: O sabahah!"

It was related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull al-Nahdi, from Qabisah and Zuhayr ibn Amr al-Hilali, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/60), Sahih Muslim no. (207), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11379).]].

The Fifth Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the people of his household, and thirty gathered, and they ate and drank. He said: "Who will take on my debts and my promises, and will be with me in Paradise, and will be my successor among my family?" A man, whom Shurayk did not name, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were a sea [...] who will undertake this?" Then the other spoke, and this was presented to his household, and Ali said: "I will."

[[al-Musnad (1/111). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Shurayk, who is trustworthy."]]

Another route, more detailed than this context: Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadhij, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, or called, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who were a group, each of whom eats a whole young camel and drinks a farq (a large measure). He said: And he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were satisfied. He said: The food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for a bowl, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched, or had not been drunk. Then he said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I have been sent to you in particular and to mankind in general, and you have seen from this verse what you have seen. Which of you will pledge allegiance to me that he will be my brother and my companion?" He said: No one rose to him. He said: I rose to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: He said: "Sit down." Then he said it three times, and each time I would rise to him, and he would say to me: "Sit down." Until in the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.

[[al-Musnad (1/159). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

A different chain, more unusual and more detailed than this one, with additional elements. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (*Proofs of Prophethood*): Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Someone who heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told me (and he asked me to keep his name secret) from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk, and lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what your Lord has commanded you, your Lord will punish you.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He called me and said: 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsfolk [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]]. I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you have been commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us, O Ali, a sheep with a sa' of food, and prepare for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib.'" [[In F: "for us".]] So I did, and they gathered before him. They were then forty men, give or take a man. Among them were his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab, the disbelieving wretch. I brought that dish to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece from it, split it with his teeth, then threw it around the sides of the dish and said: "Eat, in the name of Allah." The people ate until they were satisfied, and nothing could be seen but the traces of their fingers. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before. They ate until they were satisfied, and by Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared for us yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]], and they ate until they were satisfied. Then I gave them to drink from that cup until they were satisfied. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it and drink the like of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, indeed, by Allah, I know of no young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the affair of this world and the Hereafter."

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: "It has reached me that Ibn Ishaq heard it only from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/178).]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned something similar, but he added after his saying "I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter": "And Allah has commanded me to invite you to Him. So which of you will support me in this matter, on condition that he be my brother and such-and-such?" He said: "The people all held back from it, and I said, though I was the youngest of them in age, the most inflamed in eyes, the largest in belly, and the thinnest in shins: 'I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your minister in this.' He looked at me for a while, then said: 'Indeed, this is my brother, and such-and-such. So listen to him and obey him.'" He said: "The people rose laughing and said to Abu Talib: 'He has commanded you to listen to your son and obey him!'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/40).]]

Only Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam narrated this account in this form. He is abandoned (matruk), a liar, and a Shi'ite. Ali ibn al-Madini and others accused him of fabricating hadith, and the imams weakened him, may Allah have mercy on them.

Another chain: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us: al-Husayn ibn Isa ibn Maysarah al-Harithi related to us: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Quddus related to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food and a vessel of milk." He said: "I did so. Then he said: 'Call the Banu Hashim.'" He said: "I called them, and they were that day forty men, or forty and one man." He said: "Among them were ten who each ate a whole goat's leg with its condiment." He said: "When they brought the bowl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from its top and said: 'Eat.' They ate until they were satisfied, and it remained as it was, having lost only a little from it." He said: "Then I brought them the vessel and they drank until they were quenched, and there was a surplus. When they had finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak, but they hastened to speech and said: 'We have never seen anything like today's sorcery.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food." So I did. He said: "He gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, they hastened again and said the same thing as their first saying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said to me: 'Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food.'" [[In F: "for me" added.]] So I did. He said: "I gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened to speech and said: 'Which of you will settle my debt and be my successor in my family?'" He said: "They were silent, and al-Abbas was silent, fearing that this would consume his wealth. I was silent because of al-Abbas's age. Then he said it a second time, and al-Abbas was silent. When I saw that, I said: 'I, O Messenger of Allah.' [He said: 'You.'] [[added from F.]]" He said: "On that day I was the worst of them in appearance. I had inflamed eyes, a large belly, and thin shins."

These are multiple chains for this hadith from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. The meaning of his (ﷺ) request to his paternal uncles and their sons that they settle his debt and succeed him in his family is that, if he were killed in the way of Allah, since he feared that when he took up the burdens of warning he might be killed. When Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:67], then at that point he felt secure.

He had been guarded at first until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. At that time, none among the Banu Hashim was stronger in faith, certainty, and affirmation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Therefore he hastened ahead of them in committing to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked of them. Then after this, and Allah knows best, came his calling the people openly on al-Safa, and his warning to the clans of Quraysh in general and in particular, until he named some of his paternal uncles, aunts, and daughters, so that he might alert them to the greater by means of the lesser. That is: "I am only a warner, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path."

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi (not otherwise identified), through the chain of Amr ibn Samurah, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abd al-Wahid al-Dimashqi, who said: "I saw Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, teaching people and giving them legal rulings, while his son was beside him and his family were sitting at the side of the mosque conversing. It was said to him: 'Why do people desire what you have of knowledge, while your family sit heedless?' He said: 'Because I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The prophets are the most detached from the world, and the hardest on them are the nearest of kin." This is what Allah revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾.'" Then he said: "Indeed, the people most averse to the scholar are his own family until he departs from them." This is why Allah (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk. And lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers. But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ [[Tarikh Dimashq (10/587, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ means: in all your affairs, for indeed He is your supporter, your helper, your protector, your victor, and the one who exalts your word.

* *

His saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: He takes care of you, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are before Our eyes﴾ [al-Tur 52:48].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: to the prayer.

Ikrimah said: He sees his standing, his bowing, and his prostration.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: when you pray alone.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: that is, from your bed or your sitting place.

Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you﴾: standing, sitting, and in all your conditions.

* *

His saying: ﴿And your movements among those who prostrate﴾: Qatadah said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand, and your movements among those who prostrate﴾ means: in the prayer, He sees you alone and He sees you in congregation. This is the view of Ikrimah, Ata al-Khurasani, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Mujahid said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see those behind him just as he saw those in front of him. This is supported by what is authentically established in the hadith: "Straighten your rows, for indeed I see you from behind my back." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (723).]]

Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through two chains from Ibn Abbas that he said regarding this verse: it means His moving him from the loins of one prophet to the loins of another prophet until He brought him forth as a prophet.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ means: the All-Hearing of His servants' statements, the All-Knowing of their movements and stillness, as He says (Exalted is He): ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite of it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engrossed therein﴾ [Yunus 10:61], and the rest of the verse.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah al-Shu'ara' (26), verses 213–220:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding that He alone be worshipped, with no partner, and informing that whoever associates others with Him, He will punish him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In manuscripts F and A: "may the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him."]], to warn his closest kinsmen, i.e., those nearest to him, and that none of them will be saved except by faith in his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He also commanded him to lower his wing to those among the believing servants of Allah who follow him. As for whoever disobeys him among the creatures of Allah, whoever he may be, he should disassociate himself from him. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ This special warning does not contradict the general warning; rather it is one part of it, as He said: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and He said: ﴿So that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shura: 7], and He said: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51], and He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings with it to the righteous and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], and He said: ﴿That I may warn you with it and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], just as He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

In Sahih Muslim: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."

Many hadiths have been related concerning the revelation of this noble verse, so let us mention them:

The First Hadith:

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa and climbed upon it, then called out: "O sabahah!" The people gathered around him, some coming to him and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu Lu'ayy, if I were to inform you that there were horsemen at the foot of this mountain intending to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish all day! Did you call us only for this?" And Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4801), Sahih Muslim no. (208), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3363).]].

The Second Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." Muslim alone transmitted it [[al-Musnad (6/187) and Sahih Muslim no. (205).]].

The Third Hadith:

Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned [Quraysh] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]], addressing both the general and the specific, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. [O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. For indeed, by Allah, I possess nothing for you against Allah, except that you have a kinship which I will keep in good standing, with its moisture."

It was related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/360), Sahih Muslim no. (204), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3185).]]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." It was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Musa ibn Talhah as a mursal report, not mentioning Abu Hurayrah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/248).]]. The connected (mawsul) version is the sound one. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4771) and Sahih Muslim no. (206).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, buy yourselves from Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, and O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, buy yourselves from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you both wish."

He alone related it through this route [[al-Musnad (2/448).]]. He also alone related it, from Mu'awiyah, from Za'idah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording [[al-Musnad (2/398).]]. He also related it from Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it as a marfu' report [[al-Musnad (2/350).]].

Abu Ya'la said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Dhimam ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Banu Qusayy, O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd Manaf. I am the warner, and death is the sudden raider, and the Hour is the appointed time." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/10); Suwayd ibn Sa'id is subject to criticism.]].

The Fourth Hadith:

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq and Zuhayr ibn Amr, who both said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) climbed a rocky outcrop of a mountain, upon whose summit was a stone, and began calling out: "O Banu Abd Manaf, I am only a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy and went to warn his people, fearing they would be overtaken, so he began calling out and shouting: O sabahah!"

It was related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull al-Nahdi, from Qabisah and Zuhayr ibn Amr al-Hilali, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/60), Sahih Muslim no. (207), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11379).]].

The Fifth Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the people of his household, and thirty gathered, and they ate and drank. He said: "Who will take on my debts and my promises, and will be with me in Paradise, and will be my successor among my family?" A man, whom Shurayk did not name, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were a sea [...] who will undertake this?" Then the other spoke, and this was presented to his household, and Ali said: "I will."

[[al-Musnad (1/111). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Shurayk, who is trustworthy."]]

Another route, more detailed than this context: Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadhij, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, or called, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who were a group, each of whom eats a whole young camel and drinks a farq (a large measure). He said: And he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were satisfied. He said: The food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for a bowl, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched, or had not been drunk. Then he said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I have been sent to you in particular and to mankind in general, and you have seen from this verse what you have seen. Which of you will pledge allegiance to me that he will be my brother and my companion?" He said: No one rose to him. He said: I rose to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: He said: "Sit down." Then he said it three times, and each time I would rise to him, and he would say to me: "Sit down." Until in the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.

[[al-Musnad (1/159). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

A different chain, more unusual and more detailed than this one, with additional elements. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (*Proofs of Prophethood*): Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Someone who heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told me (and he asked me to keep his name secret) from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk, and lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what your Lord has commanded you, your Lord will punish you.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He called me and said: 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsfolk [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]]. I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you have been commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us, O Ali, a sheep with a sa' of food, and prepare for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib.'" [[In F: "for us".]] So I did, and they gathered before him. They were then forty men, give or take a man. Among them were his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab, the disbelieving wretch. I brought that dish to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece from it, split it with his teeth, then threw it around the sides of the dish and said: "Eat, in the name of Allah." The people ate until they were satisfied, and nothing could be seen but the traces of their fingers. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before. They ate until they were satisfied, and by Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared for us yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]], and they ate until they were satisfied. Then I gave them to drink from that cup until they were satisfied. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it and drink the like of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, indeed, by Allah, I know of no young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the affair of this world and the Hereafter."

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: "It has reached me that Ibn Ishaq heard it only from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/178).]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned something similar, but he added after his saying "I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter": "And Allah has commanded me to invite you to Him. So which of you will support me in this matter, on condition that he be my brother and such-and-such?" He said: "The people all held back from it, and I said, though I was the youngest of them in age, the most inflamed in eyes, the largest in belly, and the thinnest in shins: 'I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your minister in this.' He looked at me for a while, then said: 'Indeed, this is my brother, and such-and-such. So listen to him and obey him.'" He said: "The people rose laughing and said to Abu Talib: 'He has commanded you to listen to your son and obey him!'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/40).]]

Only Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam narrated this account in this form. He is abandoned (matruk), a liar, and a Shi'ite. Ali ibn al-Madini and others accused him of fabricating hadith, and the imams weakened him, may Allah have mercy on them.

Another chain: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us: al-Husayn ibn Isa ibn Maysarah al-Harithi related to us: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Quddus related to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food and a vessel of milk." He said: "I did so. Then he said: 'Call the Banu Hashim.'" He said: "I called them, and they were that day forty men, or forty and one man." He said: "Among them were ten who each ate a whole goat's leg with its condiment." He said: "When they brought the bowl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from its top and said: 'Eat.' They ate until they were satisfied, and it remained as it was, having lost only a little from it." He said: "Then I brought them the vessel and they drank until they were quenched, and there was a surplus. When they had finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak, but they hastened to speech and said: 'We have never seen anything like today's sorcery.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said: "Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food." So I did. He said: "He gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, they hastened again and said the same thing as their first saying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, then said to me: 'Prepare for me a leg of a sheep with a sa' of food.'" [[In F: "for me" added.]] So I did. He said: "I gathered them, and when they had eaten and drunk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened to speech and said: 'Which of you will settle my debt and be my successor in my family?'" He said: "They were silent, and al-Abbas was silent, fearing that this would consume his wealth. I was silent because of al-Abbas's age. Then he said it a second time, and al-Abbas was silent. When I saw that, I said: 'I, O Messenger of Allah.' [He said: 'You.'] [[added from F.]]" He said: "On that day I was the worst of them in appearance. I had inflamed eyes, a large belly, and thin shins."

He also commanded him to lower his wing to those among the believing servants of Allah who follow him. As for whoever disobeys him among the creatures of Allah, whoever he may be, he should disassociate himself from him. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ This special warning does not contradict the general warning; rather it is one part of it, as He said: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and He said: ﴿So that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shura: 7], and He said: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51], and He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings with it to the righteous and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], and He said: ﴿That I may warn you with it and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], just as He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

In Sahih Muslim: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire."

Many hadiths have been related concerning the revelation of this noble verse, so let us mention them:

The First Hadith:

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa and climbed upon it, then called out: "O sabahah!" The people gathered around him, some coming to him and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu Lu'ayy, if I were to inform you that there were horsemen at the foot of this mountain intending to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish all day! Did you call us only for this?" And Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4801), Sahih Muslim no. (208), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3363).]].

The Second Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." Muslim alone transmitted it [[al-Musnad (6/187) and Sahih Muslim no. (205).]].

The Third Hadith:

Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned [Quraysh] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]], addressing both the general and the specific, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O assembly of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. [O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. For indeed, by Allah, I possess nothing for you against Allah, except that you have a kinship which I will keep in good standing, with its moisture."

It was related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (2/360), Sahih Muslim no. (204), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3185).]]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." It was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Musa ibn Talhah as a mursal report, not mentioning Abu Hurayrah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/248).]]. The connected (mawsul) version is the sound one. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4771) and Sahih Muslim no. (206).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, buy yourselves from Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, and O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, buy yourselves from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me from my wealth whatever you both wish."

He alone related it through this route [[al-Musnad (2/448).]]. He also alone related it, from Mu'awiyah, from Za'idah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording [[al-Musnad (2/398).]]. He also related it from Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it as a marfu' report [[al-Musnad (2/350).]].

Abu Ya'la said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Dhimam ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Banu Qusayy, O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd Manaf. I am the warner, and death is the sudden raider, and the Hour is the appointed time." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/10); Suwayd ibn Sa'id is subject to criticism.]].

The Fourth Hadith:

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq and Zuhayr ibn Amr, who both said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) climbed a rocky outcrop of a mountain, upon whose summit was a stone, and began calling out: "O Banu Abd Manaf, I am only a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy and went to warn his people, fearing they would be overtaken, so he began calling out and shouting: O sabahah!"

It was related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull al-Nahdi, from Qabisah and Zuhayr ibn Amr al-Hilali, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/60), Sahih Muslim no. (207), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11379).]].

The Fifth Hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the people of his household, and thirty gathered, and they ate and drank. He said: "Who will take on my debts and my promises, and will be with me in Paradise, and will be my successor among my family?" A man, whom Shurayk did not name, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were a sea [...] who will undertake this?" Then the other spoke, and this was presented to his household, and Ali said: "I will."

[[al-Musnad (1/111). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Shurayk, who is trustworthy."]]

Another route, more detailed than this context: Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadhij, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, or called, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who were a group, each of whom eats a whole young camel and drinks a farq (a large measure). He said: And he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were satisfied. He said: The food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for a bowl, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched, or had not been drunk. Then he said: "O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I have been sent to you in particular and to mankind in general, and you have seen from this verse what you have seen. Which of you will pledge allegiance to me that he will be my brother and my companion?" He said: No one rose to him. He said: I rose to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: He said: "Sit down." Then he said it three times, and each time I would rise to him, and he would say to me: "Sit down." Until in the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.

[[al-Musnad (1/159). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/302): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

A different chain, more unusual and more detailed than this one, with additional elements. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (*Proofs of Prophethood*): Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Someone who heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told me (and he asked me to keep his name secret) from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk, and lower your wing to whoever follows you of the believers﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what your Lord has commanded you, your Lord will punish you.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He called me and said: 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsfolk [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]]. I realized that if I began with them, I would see from them what I dislike, so I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you have been commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us, O Ali, a sheep with a sa' of food, and prepare for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib.'" [[In F: "for us".]] So I did, and they gathered before him. They were then forty men, give or take a man. Among them were his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab, the disbelieving wretch. I brought that dish to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece from it, split it with his teeth, then threw it around the sides of the dish and said: "Eat, in the name of Allah." The people ate until they were satisfied, and nothing could be seen but the traces of their fingers. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before. They ate until they were satisfied, and by Allah, one of them would eat the like of it alone. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give them to drink, O Ali." So I brought that cup, and they drank from it until they were all satisfied. By Allah, one of them would drink the like of it alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "This is indeed the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" They dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. On the next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ali, prepare for us again the like of what you prepared for us yesterday of food and drink, for this man has hastened to what you heard before I could speak to the people." So I did, then I gathered them for him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did as he had done the day before [[added from F, A, and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]], and they ate until they were satisfied. Then I gave them to drink from that cup until they were satisfied. By Allah, one of them would eat the like of it and drink the like of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, indeed, by Allah, I know of no young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the affair of this world and the Hereafter."

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: "It has reached me that Ibn Ishaq heard it only from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abi Maryam, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/178).]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned something similar, but he added after his saying "I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter": "And Allah has commanded me to invite you to Him.
