The purpose of this is that the Messenger ﷺ upon whom this Qur'an was revealed is neither a soothsayer nor a poet, because his state contradicts theirs in manifest respects, as Allah said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya Sin 69], and Allah said: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger. And it is not the word of a poet—little do you believe. Nor the word of a soothsayer—little do you remember. A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqa 40-43]. Likewise He says here: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down. It is not befitting for them, nor are they able. Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying, sinful one. They cast the hearing, and most of them are liars. And the poets—the astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, mawla of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When the verse ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." The Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ and said: "You are [them]." ﴿And remember Allah much﴾ and said: "You are [them]." ﴿And defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾ and said: "You are [them]."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, through the narration of Ibn Ishaq [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/79)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Abu Usama, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu al-Hasan, mawla of Banu Nawfal, that Hassan ibn Thabit and 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when there was revealed: ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾, weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while reciting it to them, [reached]: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and said: "You are [them]" [al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak (3/488) through the route of Abu Usama].

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 26, verses 221–227 (part 2 of 2):

He also said: My father related to us, Abu Salamah related to us [[In F and A: "Abu Muslim".]], Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from 'Urwah, who said: When the verse ﴿And the poets—the misguided follow them﴾ was revealed, up to His words ﴿they say what they do not do﴾, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah knows that I am one of them." Then Allah revealed: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, up to His words ﴿will return﴾.

Likewise, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said that this is an exception from what preceded. There is no doubt that it is an exception, but this surah is Meccan, so how could the cause of revelation of this verse be the poets of the Ansar? There is room for consideration in that, and nothing has come down except transmissions with broken chains (mursalat) that cannot be relied upon. And Allah knows best. However, this exception includes the poets of the Ansar and others, and it includes whoever among the poets of the Jahiliyyah was engaged in disparaging Islam and its people, then repented, turned back, desisted, did righteous deeds, and remembered Allah much, in response to what he had previously said of evil speech. Good deeds erase evil deeds. He also praised Islam and its people in opposition to what he had previously disparaged them with, as 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ara said when he embraced Islam:

O Messenger of the King, my tongue
has mended what I had torn, when I was a destroyer.
When I was a companion of Satan in the paths of error,
and whoever inclines to his inclination is ruined.

Likewise Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who was among the people most hostile to the Prophet (ﷺ) and was his cousin, and the one who satirized him most. When he embraced Islam, no one was more beloved to him than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He would praise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after having satirized him, and would support him after having opposed him. Muslim also related this in his Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas: that Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb, when he embraced Islam, said: "O Messenger of Allah, give me three things." He said: "Yes." He said: "Mu'awiyah, make him a scribe in your presence." He said: "Yes." He said: "And appoint me to fight the disbelievers, just as I used to fight the Muslims." He said: "Yes." And he mentioned the three [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2501).]].

Therefore, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah much﴾. It was said: its meaning is that they remember Allah much in their speech. It was also said: in their poetry. Both interpretations are sound and expiate what preceded.

* *

His words: ﴿and who defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they respond to the disbelievers who used to satirize the believers. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said the same. This is like what is established in the Sahih: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hassan: "Satirize them—or he said, respond to them—and Jibril is with you" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6153), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2486), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar related to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed about poetry what He has revealed." He said: "Indeed the believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand my soul is, what you hurl at them is like the spray of arrows" [[al-Musnad (6/387).]].

* *

His words: ﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. In the Sahih, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2578), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him; its wording: "Guard against injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection."]].

Qatadah ibn Di'amah said regarding His words ﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾: he means the poets and others.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Iyas ibn Abi Tamimah related to us, saying: I was present with al-Hasan when a funeral of a Christian passed by him. Al-Hasan recited: ﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Rabah related from Safwan ibn Muhriz: that when he recited this verse, he would weep until I would say: "The cartilage of his throat has been crushed"—﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾.

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Surayj al-Iskandarani informed me [[In F and A: "related to us".]], from some of the shaykhs, that they were in the land of the Romans, and one night while they were around a fire, warming themselves or roasting [[In A: "roasting".]] over it, suddenly riders [[In F and A: "riders" (rukban).]] came toward them. They stood up to meet them, and there among them was Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd. They brought him down and he sat with them. (He said: and a companion of ours was standing and praying.) He said: until he came to this verse: ﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾. Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd said: "These are the ones who ruin the House."

It was said: what is meant by them is the people of Makkah. It was said: those who wronged among the polytheists. The sound view is that this verse is general for every wrongdoer, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: it was mentioned from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Wasiti: al-Haytham ibn Mahfuz Abu Sa'd [[In F and A: "Abu Sa'id".]] al-Nahdi related to me, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mujir related to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah related to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: My father wrote his will in two lines: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is what Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah bequeathed upon his departure from the world, at a time when the disbeliever believes, the wicked desists, and the liar tells the truth: Indeed I have appointed 'Umar ibn al-Khattab as your successor. If he is just, that is my assessment of him and my hope in him; and if he deviates and alters, then I do not know the unseen. ﴿And those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾."

End of the commentary on Surah "al-Shu'ara'". All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, addresses those among the polytheists who claimed that what the Messenger brought was not true, that it was something he invented on his own, or that a jinn companion (ra'iy min al-jinn) brought it to him. So Allah, glorified is He, cleared the honor of His Messenger of their saying and their fabrication, and made clear that what he brought was [the truth] (added from manuscripts F and A) from Allah, that it is His revelation and His inspiration, brought down by a noble, trustworthy, mighty angel, and that it is not of the kind of the devils, for they have no desire for a Qur'an this great. The devils only descend upon those who resemble them and are like them, the lying soothsayers (kuhhan, sing. kahin). For this reason Allah said: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying, sinful sorcerer.﴾ That is, I inform you. ﴿Upon every lying, sinful one﴾: that is, one who lies in his speech, and this is the afak athim (the lying, sinful one), i.e., the wicked one in his deeds. This is the one upon whom the devils descend, like the soothsayers and those who follow their way from liars and transgressors, for the devils too are liars and transgressors.

﴿They cast the hearing﴾: that is, they steal hearing from the heaven, so they hear a word of the unseen knowledge, and then they add to it a hundred lies, and then they convey it to their human allies, who speak of it, and people believe everything they say because of their truthfulness in that one word which was heard from the heaven, as this hadith confirms, as narrated by al-Bukhari, from the hadith of al-Zuhri: Yahya ibn 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he heard 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr say: 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Some people asked the Prophet ﷺ about the soothsayers, and he said: 'They are nothing.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they sometimes tell us something that turns out to be true?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'That word of truth is snatched by the jinn, who whispers it into the ear of his friend like the clucking of a hen, and they mix with it more than a hundred lies.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7561].

Al-Bukhari also said: Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah say: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels strike their wings in submission to His word, like a chain on a smooth rock. When fear is removed from their hearts, they say: 'What has your Lord said?' They say: 'The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.' Then the eavesdroppers hear it, and the eavesdroppers are [stacked] one above another like this." Sufyan described it with his hand, bending it and spreading his fingers. "So one hears the word and throws it to the one beneath him, and then that one throws it to the next beneath him, until it is thrown onto the tongue of the sorcerer or the soothsayer. Sometimes the meteor overtakes him before he throws it, and sometimes he throws it before it reaches him, and he lies with it a hundred lies. Then it is said: 'Did he not tell us on such-and-such a day such-and-such?' And he is believed because of that one word which he heard from the heaven." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4800].

Muslim narrated from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, from men of the Ansar, something close to this. It will come under His saying in Saba': ﴿until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾ [Saba' 23], God willing.

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Layth said: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, that Abu al-Aswad informed him, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The angels speak in the 'anan (and 'anan is the cloud) about a matter [that occurs] on the earth, and the devils hear the word and whisper it into the ear of the soothsayer as a flask is filled, and they add to it a hundred lies." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3288; Abu Nu'aym connected it in al-Mustakhraj through Abu Hatim al-Razi from Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, from him, as in al-Fath (6/432)].

Al-Bukhari said in another place in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, from Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, from al-Layth, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from Abu al-Aswad Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, similar to this [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2210].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, the disbelievers, the misguided among mankind and jinn follow them. Likewise Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

'Ikrima said: The two poets used to satirize one another, and a group of people would support this one, and a group would support that one, so Allah revealed: ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Qutayba narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from Yuhannas, mawla of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Sa'id, who said: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-'Araj, a poet appeared reciting poetry. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seize the devil—or hold back the devil—for for one of you to have his belly filled with pus is better for him than to have it filled with poetry." [Musnad, 3/8].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley?﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: in every vain talk they plunge.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: in every kind of speech. Likewise Mujahid and others said.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: By Allah, we have seen their valleys in which they wander: sometimes in the insult of so-and-so, and sometimes in the praise of so-and-so.

Qatada said: The poet praises a people with falsehood and blames a people with falsehood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾: al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: There were two men in the time of the Messenger of Allah, one of them from the Ansar and the other from another tribe, and they satirized one another. Each of them had misguided followers from his people, who were the foolish ones. So Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: most of what they say is lies.

What Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said is the reality of the matter, for poets boast of sayings and deeds that never came from them, and they inflate themselves with what is not theirs. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed concerning whether a poet who confesses in his poetry to something that requires a prescribed punishment (hadd) is to be punished on the basis of that confession, since "they say what they do not do," on two views. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Muhammad ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat, and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in the book al-Fukaha mentioned that the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed al-Nu'man ibn 'Adi ibn Nadla over Maysan (a land of Basra), and he used to compose poetry, and he said:

Does the beautiful woman know that her husband
is in Maysan, being given drink from glass and jars?
When I wish, the peasants of the village sing to me,
and a dancing girl sways on every tiptoe.
If you are my drinking companion, then give me to drink from the larger [cup],
and do not give me to drink from the smaller, chipped one.
Perhaps the Commander of the Faithful will be displeased
by our carousing in the ruined palace.

When this reached the Commander of the Faithful, he said: "By Allah, that indeed displeases me. Whoever meets him, let him inform him that I have dismissed him." And he wrote to him: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing. Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty. There is no deity but Him; to Him is the final return﴾ [Ghafir 1-3]. To proceed: your saying has reached me:
Perhaps the Commander of the Faithful will be displeased
by our carousing in the ruined palace.
By Allah, it indeed displeases me, and I have dismissed you." When he came to 'Umar, he reproached him with this poetry. He said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, I have never drunk it, and that poetry was only something that overflowed on my tongue." 'Umar said: "I think so. But by Allah, you will never work for me in any position again, after what you said." [The verses are in Ibn Hisham's al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/266) and Ibn Sa'd's al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (4/140)].

It is not mentioned that he was punished for drinking, though his poetry implicated him, because "they say what they do not do." Rather, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, censured him, blamed him for that, and dismissed him because of it. For this reason it came in the hadith: "For one of you to have his belly filled with pus, which would wear him down, is better for him than to have it filled with poetry" [narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2257, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him].

The purpose of this is that the Messenger ﷺ upon whom this Qur'an was revealed is neither a soothsayer nor a poet, because his state contradicts theirs in manifest respects, as Allah said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya Sin 69], and Allah said: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger. And it is not the word of a poet—little do you believe. Nor the word of a soothsayer—little do you remember. A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqa 40-43]. Likewise He says here: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down. It is not befitting for them, nor are they able. Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying, sinful one. They cast the hearing, and most of them are liars. And the poets—the astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, mawla of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When the verse ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." The Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ and said: "You are [them]." ﴿And remember Allah much﴾ and said: "You are [them]." ﴿And defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾ and said: "You are [them]."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, through the narration of Ibn Ishaq [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/79)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Abu Usama, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu al-Hasan, mawla of Banu Nawfal, that Hassan ibn Thabit and 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when there was revealed: ﴿And the poets—the astray follow them﴾, weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while reciting it to them, [reached]: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and said: "You are [them]" [al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak (3/488) through the route of Abu Usama].

He said: until he came to this verse: ﴿and those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾. Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd said: "These are the ones who ruin the House."

It was said: what is meant by them is the people of Makkah. It was said: those who wronged among the polytheists. The sound view is that this verse is general for every wrongdoer, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: it was mentioned from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Wasiti: al-Haytham ibn Mahfuz Abu Sa'd [[In F and A: "Abu Sa'id".]] al-Nahdi related to me, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mujir related to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah related to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: My father wrote his will in two lines: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is what Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah bequeathed upon his departure from the world, at a time when the disbeliever believes, the wicked desists, and the liar tells the truth: Indeed I have appointed 'Umar ibn al-Khattab as your successor. If he is just, that is my assessment of him and my hope in him; and if he deviates and alters, then I do not know the unseen. ﴿And those who wronged will know what kind of return they will be returned to﴾."

End of the commentary on Surah "al-Shu'ara'". All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
